clarifications: What if one array is empty? The median is the median of the non-empty array.
Can the arrays have duplicate elements? Yes, duplicates are allowed.
What if both arrays are empty? This situation is not allowed by the constraints.
Should the input arrays be modified? No, the input arrays should not be modified.
What type should the median be returned as? Return the median as a float.
What if the total number of elements is even? The median is the average of the two middle numbers.
Are the arrays always sorted? Yes, both input arrays are sorted.
expectedApproaches: Merge and sort approach with O((m+n) log(m+n)) complexity.
Binary search on the smaller array with O(log(min(m,n))) complexity.
solutions: Perform a binary search on the smaller array to partition both arrays such that the left partition contains the same number of elements as the right partition. Adjust the partitions until the maximum of the left partition is less than or equal to the minimum of the right partition. Calculate the median based on the partition sizes and values.
commonMistakes: Using a simple merge and sort approach, which is not O(log(m+n)).
Incorrectly handling cases where one array is empty.
Failing to correctly calculate the median when the total number of elements is even.
